root_cause: The Awesomplete widget creates suggestion list items with `tabindex="0"`, making them part of the browser's tab order. When the suggestion list is open, pressing Tab moves focus into the list (to the first item) instead of continuing to the next form field (dietary input). This violates WCAG 2.1.1 (keyboard accessibility) and 2.4.3 (focus order).
repair_strategy: Change the `tabindex` attribute of generated list items from `0` to `-1`. This removes them from the sequential tab order while preserving their accessibility via `aria-activedescendant` for arrow-key navigation. The combobox input remains the only focusable element in the widget, so Tab naturally advances to the next focusable element outside the widget.
expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab while the city combobox's suggestion list is open will now move focus directly to the dietary requirements input, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (keyboard) and 2.4.3 (focus order). Arrow-key navigation and Enter selection continue to work via aria-activedescendant.
functional_risks: Screen readers that rely on list items being focusable (e.g., Talkback) may no longer receive focus on individual options; however, the combobox pattern uses aria-activedescendant for announcement, which is the standard approach.
If any custom code depends on list items being in the tab order, it will break; but the default configuration has tabSelect=false, so impact is minimal.
verification_requirements: After typing 'Ber' in the city field, pressing Tab must move focus to the dietary input (focus assertion).
The suggestion list must remain open and navigable with arrow keys; Enter must select a suggestion.
The city field's value should remain unchanged after Tab press.
Regression guard: choosing a suggestion with arrow keys and Enter must still work.
